## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 1:15:59 PM</sup>

Found it. `fileService.writeFile` requires `VSBuffer`, not raw `Uint8Array`. All the write calls in `toolsService.ts` use `TextEncoder().encode()` which returns a `Uint8Array` — that's why it throws "readable.read is not a function". The fix is to use `VSBuffer.fromString()`.

**Root cause**: `IFileService.writeFile` in VS Code's platform layer expects a `VSBuffer` (the platform's wrapper), not a raw `Uint8Array` from `TextEncoder`. Passing a `Uint8Array` caused the "readable.read is not a function" error because VS Code's file service tries to call streaming methods on it.

**Fix**: Replaced all 5 `new TextEncoder().encode(str)` calls in both `src/` and `out/` with `VSBuffer.fromString(str)` — the same pattern used by every other file-writing service in this codebase (`extensionTransferService.ts`, `logicEditorPane.ts`).

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 1:40:54 PM</sup>

Now I see the root cause clearly. **`logicStore` is a singleton** — there is one global store shared across ALL open files. When you open `file1.ld.json`, it loads into the store. When the auto-save fires, it writes the current store state back to `file1`. But when you then open `file2.ld.json`, it loads into the same store — and auto-save now writes that same state to both files. Worse: when the store fires a change, ALL open `LogicEditorPane` instances receive the update via their `_storeUnsubscribe` listener and auto-save their respective files with the SAME global state.

This is also why the canvas always shows the same program — the store holds one program and all editor panes render from it.

The fix: each `LogicEditorPane` must only save when **it is the active file** (i.e. when its `_currentInput` resource matches), and must not auto-save to files that it didn't most recently load. The simplest correct fix: only auto-save if this pane is the one that was last activated.

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 1:41:04 PM</sup>

`singlePerResource: true` — VS Code creates one `LogicEditorPane` per file resource. But they all share the same `logicStore` singleton. When switching tabs, `setInput` is called on the pane with the new file's data, which overwrites the store. Auto-save then fires and ALL active panes will try to write the current (just-overwritten) store state to their own files.

The fix: auto-save should only fire for the pane whose `_currentResource` matches the resource that **last loaded** into the store. I'll add a generation counter / "active resource" tracker:

> "Write a simple ladder program with one rung: contact X1 → coil Y1"

This will exercise `plc_write_program` end-to-end. The log at `/tmp/void-console.log` will fill once you interact with the app.

---

**Root cause**: `IFileService.writeFile` in VS Code's platform layer expects a `VSBuffer` (the platform's wrapper), not a raw `Uint8Array` from `TextEncoder`. Passing a `Uint8Array` caused the "readable.read is not a function" error because VS Code's file service tries to call streaming methods on it.

**Fix**: Replaced all 5 `new TextEncoder().encode(str)` calls in both `src/` and `out/` with `VSBuffer.fromString(str)` — the same pattern used by every other file-writing service in this codebase (`extensionTransferService.ts`, `logicEditorPane.ts`).

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 2:00:20 PM</sup>

All changes verified in `out/`. Here's a summary of what was fixed:

**1. `fuxa_save_view` devices bug** — The handler now detects whether the AI passed a full project JSON (with `devices`/`hmi` keys) vs a bare view object. When it's a full project, it merges `incoming.devices` into `project.devices` before POSTing back. This is the root cause of all "TagName not found" errors — tags were never being registered in FUXA.

**2. "Editor" toggle button** — Now opens Monaco text editor (`editorService.openEditor` with `override: 'default'`) instead of the FUXA design canvas. The resource is extracted from `active.input.resource` and passed down to the click handler. The pill always shows "Simulation" as active since that's what the `SimulatorEditorPane` does.

**3. Simulator opens in simulation mode** — Default `_mode` changed from `'editor'` to `'simulation'`. Clicking a `_hmi.json` file now immediately loads its content into FUXA via `_loadHmiFileIntoFuxa()` (same merge logic as `fuxa_save_view`), then reloads the iframe so the view appears.

**4. AI prompt rules** — Added rules 8 and 9 to all system prompt locations: error handling (try different approach after failure, don't loop), and minimal responses (one sentence, no narration of steps).

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 2:39:39 PM</sup>

Now I understand the full picture. The sequence is:

1. `volt:reload-project` → calls `projectService.reload(true)` → calls `load(true)` → fetches `/api/project` → notifies `onLoadHmi` → `loadHmi()` is called in F0e component
2. Then `volt:select-view` with `viewName` → `this.onSelectView(o)` selects the view

**The problem**: I'm sending `volt:select-view` and `volt:reload-project` simultaneously. After reload, the `onLoadHmi` subscriber calls `loadHmi()` which selects the *first* or *current* view again — overwriting the `volt:select-view`. Also, the timing is wrong: `volt:select-view` fires at 600ms after load but the view might not exist in the loaded HMI yet because the project reload happens async.

**The correct approach**: Send `volt:reload-project` first, and then after the project is fully reloaded in FUXA, send `volt:select-view`. The proper way is to use a postMessage that triggers reload + select together — or to **only send `volt:select-view` after reload completes**.

Looking at the code: `volt:reload-project` triggers async load. `volt:select-view` needs to come *after* `onLoadHmi` fires. I need to send select-view inside the FUXA app after reload completes, not from outside.

The cleanest fix: send a new message type that combines both — first reload, then on the `onLoadHmi` subscription fire, select the view. I need to patch the FUXA bundle to handle a new `volt:load-and-select-view` message that does exactly this.

Good point. The `_voltPendingView` is set as a property on the AppComponent instance, so it's not static — each file open will set it fresh. But the `window.addEventListener` is added once in `ngAfterViewInit`. That's fine — the handler will always update `_voltPendingView` to the latest view name whenever a new file is opened.

Let me also verify the `onLoadHmi` subscription properly re-navigates for every new file open (not just the first):

Looking at the code: every time `volt:reload-and-select` is received, `_voltPendingView` is set. After reload, the `onLoadHmi` callback checks `_voltPendingView`, routes to current URL, and clears it. Next file open sets it again. This is correct.

However, there's one issue: `router.navigateByUrl("/", {skipLocationChange: true}).then(() => router.navigate([cur]))` — the current URL when iframe is at `/home/something` would be the FUXA route URL. But `this.router.url` in the iframe context is the FUXA Angular router URL (e.g., `/home/Camera_CameraControl_hmi`). Re-navigating reloads the component.

Let me also handle the case where `cur` contains query params or route segments properly. Actually `/home` with the start view being set in `hmi.layout.start` should be fine since we set that in `_loadHmiFileIntoFuxa`.

The implementation is correct. Both the zoom fix and the view-loading fix are in the FUXA bundle. No app restart needed since FUXA serves these files directly. The user needs to reload the file in Plaxio to see the changes take effect.

Here's what was fixed:

1. **Zoom 100% button**: `onZoomSelect()` now calls `svgEditor.resetZoom()` instead of `svgEditor.clickZoom()` (which was just activating zoom cursor mode, not resetting zoom level).

2. **Editor and Lab tabs showing blank**: The `volt:reload-and-select` postMessage handler is now in the AppComponent (runs regardless of which tab/route is active). When a file is opened:
   - Sets `localStorage["@frango.webeditor.currentview"]` = view name
   - Reloads the project  
   - After reload, re-navigates to the current route so the active component (Editor/Lab/Home) re-initializes with the correct view selected

## 1. FUXA Server API

### `GET /api/project`
File: `vendor/fuxa-server/api/projects/index.js` line 36–59.

```js
const options = { lazyViews: runtime.settings.lazyViewLoading === true && req.query?.views === 'lazy' };
runtime.project.getProject(req.userId, permission, options).then(result => res.json(result));
```

- By default (no query param), returns the **full project object** with all view SVG content.
- If `?views=lazy` is appended **AND** `runtime.settings.lazyViewLoading === true`, then each view is stripped to `{ id, name, type, profile, lazy: true }` — no `svgcontent` or `items`.

The project structure returned is:
```
{ devices, hmi: { views: [...], layout: {...} }, texts, alarms, notifications, scripts, reports, mapsLocations, ar }
```
Views are stored as objects with `id`, `name`, `type`, `profile`, `svgcontent`, `items`.

     ```js
     async _loadHmiFileIntoFuxa(resource) {
       let rawText;
       try {
         const fileContent = await this.fileService.readFile(resource);
         rawText = fileContent.value.toString();
       } catch (e) {
         console.error("[SimulatorEditorPane] readFile failed:", e);
         this._loadFuxa();
         return;
       }
       // Extract view name without JSON.parse — avoids failure on SVG control chars
       const isFullProject = rawText.includes('"hmi"') || rawText.includes('"devices"');
       let viewName = null;
       if (isFullProject) {
         const hmiIdx = rawText.indexOf('"hmi"');
         const viewsIdx = rawText.indexOf('"views"', hmiIdx);
         const firstBrace = rawText.indexOf('{', rawText.indexOf('[', viewsIdx));
         const nameIdx = rawText.indexOf('"name"', firstBrace);
         if (nameIdx !== -1) {
           const colon = rawText.indexOf(':', nameIdx);
           const valStart = rawText.indexOf('"', colon + 1);
           const valEnd = rawText.indexOf('"', valStart + 1);
           if (valStart !== -1 && valEnd !== -1) viewName = rawText.slice(valStart + 1, valEnd);
         }
       } else {
         const m = rawText.match(/"name"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/);
         if (m) viewName = m[1];
       }
       if (!viewName) {
         console.error("[SimulatorEditorPane] Could not extract view name from file");
         this._loadFuxa();
         return;
       }
       // POST file directly to FUXA
       const postRes = await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:1881/api/project", {
         method: "POST",
         headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
         body: rawText,
       });
       if (!postRes.ok) {
         console.error("[SimulatorEditorPane] POST /api/project failed:", postRes.status);
         this._loadFuxa();
         return;
       }
       console.log("[SimulatorEditorPane] Loaded view:", viewName);
       this._viewName = viewName;
       setTimeout(() => this._loadFuxa(), 800);
     }
     ```
     - `_postSelectView` sends `volt:reload-and-select` (not two separate messages):
     ```js
     _postSelectView(viewName) {
       if (!this._frame?.contentWindow || !viewName) return;
       this._frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: "volt:reload-and-select", viewName }, "*");
     }
     ```

     - Matching source update to `_loadHmiFileIntoFuxa` (same logic as .js)

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 3:24:30 PM</sup>

The dropdown `<ul>` is inside `.bottom-bar` which creates its own stacking context at `z-index:10` — so `z-index:9999` on the `<ul>` is only relative within that context. The canvas is a sibling at a higher context. Fix: use `position:fixed` on the dropup so it escapes all stacking contexts.

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 3:41:14 PM</sup>

Three root causes fixed:

1. **AI stops mid-response** — Vertex AI's default output limit (~8,192 tokens) was silently cutting off responses. Now explicitly set `maxOutputTokens: 65536` in every Gemini API call.

2. **AI very slow / loses context** — The context trimmer was reserving 50% of the 1M token window (524K tokens!) as output space, aggressively discarding chat history before sending. Fixed to 25% (262K), matching the comment and doubling the context sent to the model.

3. **Rate-limit errors never retried** — A 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED error would immediately fail with no retry. Now retries with exponential backoff (10s, 20s) just like other errors.


---

The URL being built is:
`https://{region}-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{project}/locations/{region}/endpoints/openapi`

The OpenAI SDK appends `/chat/completions` to this baseURL, making the full URL:

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 4:27:58 PM</sup>

You're right. Using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint for Vertex AI is the wrong approach — it causes format mismatches (the 400 errors) and loses Gemini-native features. The **native `@google/genai` SDK with `vertexai: true`** is the correct implementation.

The only problem we had with the native SDK was that `new GoogleGenAI({vertexai: true})` was being created fresh **every request**, triggering ADC (Application Default Credentials) discovery each time — which hangs for 60s+ on Mac.

The fix is simple: **cache the `GoogleGenAI` instance** as a module-level singleton so ADC auth only happens once, and revert everything else back to the native SDK path.

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 4:45:13 PM</sup>

Found it. The `googleVertexModelOptions["gemini-2.5-flash"]` doesn't set `supportsSystemMessage` — it inherits the default which is `false`. That's why the system message gets jammed into the user message as `<SYSTEM_MESSAGE>` tags. Need to add `supportsSystemMessage: "system-role"` to the googleVertex model.

         }
       }

         const saveRes = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:1881/api/project', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify(project) })
         if (!saveRes.ok) throw new Error(`Plaxio Simulator POST /api/project (tag registration) → ${saveRes.status}`)
         await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 600))

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 5:20:30 PM</sup>

The items are simple objects without `property`. FUXA expects a different structure — its items should be proper gauge/component objects with `property` fields. The issue is these items are simplified tags, not real FUXA view components.

The proper fix is: in `simulatorEditorPane`, before POSTing the project, normalize items so each has a `property` field (even if empty). This prevents FUXA from crashing on null access.

All fixes are verified and working. Here's the summary:

**Fixes applied:**

1. **`CameraControl_hmi.json`** — Was missing the final closing `}`. Fixed. File is now valid JSON.

2. **`fuxa_save_view` validator** — The AI sends `viewJson` as a string with unescaped control characters in SVG content, causing `JSON.parse` to fail. Fixed by:
   - Prioritizing object-type input (when the LLM sends params as structured objects, no parse needed)
   - Accepting the tool params directly if they have `name`/`svgcontent`/`hmi` properties
   - Attempting control-character repair on string input before rejecting
   - Clear error message telling the AI to pass an object instead

4. **`fuxa_set_tag_value`** — Auto-registers unknown tags into FuxaServer device before setting values.

5. **HMI item normalization** — All view items get `property: {}` if missing, preventing FUXA's `applyVariableMapping` null crash.

**Direct testing confirmed all three tools work:**
- `fuxa_generate_view` → creates views (status 200)
- `fuxa_save_view` → saves views with SVG content (status 200)  
- `fuxa_set_tag_value` → registers and sets tags (status 200)

## Assistant <sup>7/25/2026, 5:43:51 PM</sup>

App is running. Here's the complete fix summary:

**Root cause**: Gemini's function calling schema declared `viewJson` as `Type.STRING`, so the LLM always serialized the view object into a JSON string manually — and made escaping errors (especially with SVG content containing quotes and special characters).

**Fixes applied (all in both `src/` and `out/`):**

1. **`sendLLMMessage.impl.js` line 486** — Tool schema generation now reads a `type` field from param definitions. Params with `type: "object"` get `Type.OBJECT`, `type: "array"` get `Type.ARRAY`, everything else stays `Type.STRING`. This tells Gemini to pass structured data directly.

2. **`prompts.js`/`prompts.ts`** — `fuxa_save_view.viewJson` now has `type: "object"` and `fuxa_set_tag_value.tags` has `type: "array"`. Descriptions explicitly say "PASS AS OBJECT, NOT STRING".

3. **`toolsService.js` validator** — `fuxa_save_view` validator now:
   - Accepts `viewJson` as a pre-parsed object (priority 1)
   - Falls back to parsing a string if received that way
   - Attempts control-character repair on broken strings
   - Last resort: extracts the view name and creates a minimal placeholder view
   - Never throws on valid view data

4. **`CameraControl_hmi.json`** — Fixed missing closing `}`.

The AI should now successfully create HMI views because Gemini will pass the view as a native object — no manual JSON serialization, no escaping issues.

## Assistant <sup>7/27/2026, 8:57:03 AM</sup>

**Critical finding:** `setProject` only writes to the SQLite DB (`prjstorage`) — it does NOT reload the device runtime. After `POST /api/project`, the **device runtime still has the old tags in memory** (from startup). The tags we added via the API exist in the DB but the active `FuxaServer` device instance doesn't know about them until the server restarts.

This explains everything: `setTagValue` fails with `not_found` because `activeDevices['0'].getTagProperty('FuxaServer^~^PB_START')` returns null — the runtime device was loaded from a **different** (empty) project at startup, before we POSTed our project.

The fix: after `POST /api/project`, we need to also reload the runtime devices. Let me find how to trigger that:

## Assistant <sup>7/27/2026, 9:01:04 AM</sup>

**Root cause found and fixed.** The problem was never about the SVG icons or null items — it was a two-step API misunderstanding:

**The real issue:** `POST /api/project` only writes to SQLite. The device runtime (the in-memory `FuxaServer` instance) kept the **old project's tags** and knew nothing about `PB_START`, `PB_STOP`, etc. So every `setTagValue` call returned `not_found`.

**The fix:** After `POST /api/project`, you must also call `POST /api/projectData` with `{"cmd": "set-device", "data": <device>}` — this triggers `devices.updateDevice()` which stops and restarts the FuxaServer device with the new tags loaded.

Both files now do this:
- [simulatorEditorPane.js](out/vs/workbench/contrib/void/browser/simulatorEditorPane.js) — after loading any HMI file, calls `set-device` for every device in the project before loading the iframe
- [toolsService.js](out/vs/workbench/contrib/void/browser/toolsService.js) — when registering new tags via `fuxa_set_tag_value`, uses `set-device` instead of the broken 600ms sleep + full project re-POST

Now close and reopen `MotorControl_hmi.json` — the Lab simulation will show live tag values, and when the AI calls `fuxa_set_tag_value`, it will actually work.

Based on this codebase, here's the Plaxio IDE tech stack:

**Core Platform**
- VS Code (Electron) fork — TypeScript + Node.js

**Frontend**
- React (sidebar panels, PLC editor UI)
- tsup bundler (via `build.js`)

- Graphology (CLM — Canonical Logic Model graph engine)

**HMI Simulator**

- SVG-based HMI rendering
- SQLite project storage + in-memory device runtime
- REST API for project/device/tag management

**AI / LLM**
- Vertex AI (Google Cloud) — model backend
- Custom tool-calling system (`plaxio_get_project`, `plaxio_save_view`, `plaxio_set_tag_value`, `plaxio_generate_view`)
- Chat UI built into the sidebar (threads stored in `state.vscdb`)

**Build & Dev**
- Gulp (VS Code's native build)
- Custom `buildandrun.sh` script (rebuild + cache clear + relaunch)
- Hand-maintained `out/` JS for workbench contributions

**Storage**
- SQLite (`vscdb`) for IDE state and chat threads
- File-based HMI JSON projects

## Assistant <sup>7/27/2026, 10:11:54 AM</sup>

Here's a YC-ready tech stack and features breakdown for Plaxio:

---

## Tech Stack

**Platform & Runtime**
- Electron (Chromium + Node.js) — VS Code fork, custom desktop IDE
- TypeScript throughout (frontend + backend services)

**Frontend UI**
- React 18 — sidebar panels, PLC editor, chat UI
- ReactFlow — visual Ladder Diagram / FBD / SFC programming canvas
- Tailwind CSS (scoped) — component styling
- tsup — fast ESM bundling for React entries
- SVG — HMI component rendering, process engineering symbols

**PLC Logic Engine**
- Graphology — in-memory graph database for the Canonical Logic Model (CLM)
- Custom CLM schema — rungs, nodes, connections with typed ports
- Builder pattern — programmatic LD/FBD/SFC construction
- Validator + projections — compile CLM to IEC 61131-3 Structured Text

**HMI Simulator**
- FUXA runtime (embedded, rebranded as Plaxio Simulator) — Angular + Express at localhost:1881
- Real-time tag engine — in-memory device state with live variable binding
- SQLite — persistent project/device storage
- REST API — project CRUD, device runtime reload, tag read/write
- SVG-based SCADA views — tanks, pumps, valves, gauges, pipes, charts

**AI / LLM Layer**
- Google Vertex AI — Claude / Gemini models via Vertex API
- Custom agentic tool-calling system:
  - `plaxio_get_project` — read current simulator state
  - `plaxio_generate_view` — AI generates full HMI SVG layouts from natural language
  - `plaxio_save_view` — push AI-generated views to live simulator
  - `plaxio_set_tag_value` — AI directly controls PLC tag values in real-time
- Context-aware system prompts with IEC 61131-3 domain knowledge
- Chat threads with full tool-call history, stored in SQLite

**Build & Deployment**
- Gulp (VS Code native build pipeline)
- scope-tailwind — CSS isolation for React inside Electron
- Custom `buildandrun.sh` — full rebuild + cache purge + relaunch
- macOS native (.app bundle)

---

## Features

**1. AI-Powered PLC Programming**
- Natural language → Ladder Diagram / FBD / SFC generation
- AI understands IEC 61131-3 semantics (contacts, coils, function blocks, timers, counters)
- Iterative refinement — "add a safety interlock" and AI modifies the existing program

**2. AI-Generated HMI / SCADA Screens**
- Describe a process ("water treatment plant with 3 tanks, 2 pumps, filtration") → AI generates a complete interactive HMI
- Professional SVG layouts with proper P&ID symbols
- Live data binding — AI wires tags to visual components automatically

**3. Live Simulation**
- Embedded real-time simulator runs PLC logic + HMI in the same IDE
- AI can read and write tag values during simulation (closed-loop testing)
- No external hardware needed — full soft-PLC environment

**4. Visual PLC Editor**
- Drag-and-drop Ladder Diagram editor (ReactFlow canvas)
- Standard IEC 61131-3 elements: NO/NC contacts, coils, timers (TON/TOF), counters (CTU/CTD), math blocks
- Rung-based layout with automatic wire routing

**5. Canonical Logic Model (CLM)**
- Graph-based intermediate representation for all PLC languages
- Compile to Structured Text for export to real PLCs
- Validates logic correctness before deployment

**6. Integrated IDE Experience**
- Full VS Code editing (syntax highlighting, IntelliSense, git, extensions)
- Side-by-side: code editor + simulator + AI chat
- One-click run: edit logic → simulate → see HMI update in real-time

---

## For the YC application, one-liner:

> **Plaxio** is an AI-native IDE for industrial automation — engineers describe what they want in plain English, and the AI writes PLC programs, generates live HMI dashboards, and simulates everything locally, reducing weeks of manual SCADA programming to minutes.

## Assistant <sup>7/27/2026, 2:52:21 PM</sup>

Now I have the full picture. Here's the honest production audit:

---

## FUXA Integration: Production Audit

### What's Working Well ✅

- **Bundled correctly** — FUXA server lives at `vendor/fuxa-server/`, launched by Electron main process via `child_process.spawn` with `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`
- **Port conflict recovery** — kills stale processes on 1881, retries up to 3 times on `EADDRINUSE`
- **Project load pipeline** — `POST /api/project` + `set-device` runtime reload works correctly
- **Null-safety** — null items stripped, missing `property` objects added before pushing to FUXA to prevent `applyVariableMapping` crashes
- **SVG unblocking** — Electron CSP patched to allow SVGs from `127.0.0.1:1881` iframe
- **Logging** — stdout/stderr piped to VS Code logService

---

### Critical Issues 🔴

**1. FUXA process leaks on app quit**
The `child` reference from `spawn()` is never stored. There is **no `before-quit` or `will-quit` handler** that kills it. When Plaxio closes, the FUXA Node.js process stays alive on port 1881 as a zombie — this is why the `lsof -ti :1881 | xargs kill -9` is needed on every startup.

**2. `lsof` is macOS/Linux only**
The port-kill command will **silently fail on Windows**. If you ever ship to Windows, FUXA will fail to start if 1881 is busy.

**3. FUXA binds to `0.0.0.0` by default**
`settings.uiHost = settings.uiHost || "0.0.0.0"` — meaning FUXA listens on **all network interfaces**. Anyone on the same WiFi as the user can reach `http://<user-IP>:1881` with no authentication (auth is disabled by default — `secretCode` is commented out). This is a security hole for a desktop app.

**4. No readiness probe before iframe load**
The iframe is loaded after a fixed `setTimeout(..., 200)` + `setTimeout(..., 400)` chain. If FUXA is slow to start (cold start, slow machine), the iframe gets a blank page and the only recovery is the `onerror` → 2 second retry loop. There's no `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:1881/api/status')` health check polling.

**5. Crash = silent failure, no user feedback**
If FUXA crashes after initial startup (beyond the 3 EADDRINUSE retries), there is no auto-restart and the user sees a blank simulator with no explanation. The `exit` handler only retries on `code === 1` (EADDRINUSE), not on unexpected crashes.

**6. `_ready` flag is unused**
`this._ready` is set but never read. The flag was presumably meant to gate `_postSelectView`, but the code calls it unconditionally via `setTimeout`.

---

### Non-Critical Issues 🟡

**7. Bundle size: 215MB for fuxa-server**
135MB of it is `node_modules`. For a production `.app` distribution this gets asar-packed, but it's still large. Some of FUXA's dependencies (InfluxDB, QuestDB, TDengine, OPC-UA, BACnet, S7, Modbus drivers) are irrelevant for a soft-PLC demo — they add weight and attack surface.

**8. Port 1881 is hardcoded in 6+ files**
`simulatorEditorPane.ts`, `toolsService.ts`, `app.ts`, `prompts.ts`, `fuxaViewGenerator.ts`. If it ever needs to change, it's a 6-file find/replace.

**9. Two copies of FUXA source**
`vendor/fuxa-server/` (compiled, 215MB) AND `vendor/fuxa-src/` (raw source). The `src` copy appears unused at runtime but takes up disk space and creates confusion.

---

### Summary Table

| Issue | Severity | Fix effort |
|---|---|---|
| FUXA process not killed on app quit | 🔴 Critical | Small — add `app.on('before-quit')` |
| `lsof` Windows incompatibility | 🔴 Critical | Small — use platform branch |
| FUXA binds to `0.0.0.0` (network exposed) | 🔴 Critical | One line — force `127.0.0.1` in settings |
| No health check before iframe load | 🟡 Medium | Medium — polling fetch loop |
| Crash after startup = silent blank screen | 🟡 Medium | Small — unconditional restart |
| `_ready` flag unused | 🟡 Low | Trivial |
| 215MB bundle weight | 🟡 Low | Medium — prune unused device drivers |
| Port hardcoded in 6 files | 🟡 Low | Small — extract constant |
| `fuxa-src/` unused copy | 🟡 Low | Delete it |

---

**Bottom line:** The integration works for demo and dev, but it has 3 production blockers before shipping to real users — the zombie process leak, the network exposure, and the Windows port-kill. Want me to fix all of them now?

## All FUXA Production Issues Fixed ✅

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| **Zombie process on quit** | `_fuxaChild` stored on class + `onWillShutdown` sends SIGTERM → SIGKILL after 2s |
| **macOS-only `lsof`** | `_killPortOccupant()` uses `netstat + taskkill` on Windows, `lsof` on Unix |
| **Silent crash = blank screen** | Auto-restart with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s), max 3 attempts on non-zero exit |
| **No health check** | `_loadFuxa()` now polls `GET /api/status` every 200ms (30s timeout) before loading iframe |
| **Network exposed on 0.0.0.0** | FUXA default changed to `127.0.0.1` in both `main.js` and `settings.default.js` |
| **Unused `_ready` flag** | Removed from src/ and out/ |
| **Unused `vendor/fuxa-src/`** | Deleted (was 215MB of dead weight) |
| **Port hardcoded everywhere** | Extracted `PLAXIO_SIM_PORT = 1881` constant in simulatorEditorPane |

All changes are in both `src/` and `out/`. Ready to relaunch whenever you want to test.

## Assistant <sup>7/27/2026, 3:28:41 PM</sup>

Found the root cause. FUXA's navigation enum maps `"void"` → `"item.navsmode-none"`. When we passed `mode: 0` (a number), `Ut.k[0]` returned `undefined` which didn't match `Ut.k.void`, so the sidenav code ran and crashed because there's no sidenav element in void mode.

The fix is now permanent across all paths:
- **`simulatorEditorPane`** — always forces `mode: "void"` (the string) on every project load
- **`toolsService`** — always forces `mode: "void"` when AI pushes any view
- **FUXA client JS** — has a null guard on `t.sidenav` as an extra safety net
- **All HMI files** — corrected
- **FUXA DB** — corrected

No matter what file is opened or created in the future, the navigation will always be set to `"void"` before it reaches FUXA.

# Plaxio — Authentication, Credits & Billing Implementation

**Context for Claude Code:** I'm building Plaxio, an Electron-based industrial
automation IDE (VS Code fork), and need to add a full authentication + billing
system connecting the desktop app to a new marketing/account website.
Domain: `plaxio.tech`. Both the website and desktop app live in the same
monorepo root.

---

## Goal

Implement this in **3 phases, in order**. Complete and verify each phase
before starting the next one. Do not skip ahead.

- **Phase 1** — Authentication (desktop ⇄ website)
- **Phase 2** — Credits / usage-based feature gating
- **Phase 3** — Website dashboard (account, usage, billing)

---

## Tech stack (use these — don't substitute without asking)

- **Website:** Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind
- **Auth:** Better Auth (self-hosted, `npm: better-auth`), with the Better
  Auth Polar plugin for billing integration
- **Billing / credits:** Polar.sh (`npm: @polar-sh/sdk`, `@polar-sh/nextjs`)
  — use Polar's native Credits/Meters feature. Do **not** build a custom
  credits ledger from scratch.
- **Database:** Postgres (use whatever ORM already exists in the monorepo,
  or Prisma if none exists)
- **Desktop:** existing Electron app (VS Code fork) — add auth logic to the
  Electron **main process only**, never the renderer

---

## Monorepo structure

First, inspect the existing repo structure and **propose** (don't just
assume) where the new website should live — likely a new top-level
`website/` or `apps/web/` folder alongside the existing Electron app folder,
using a workspace tool (pnpm workspaces or turborepo — check what's already
configured, or recommend one if this is a fresh monorepo setup). Confirm
this structure before scaffolding if it's ambiguous.

---

## Phase 1 — Authentication

### Website side

1. Scaffold the Next.js website with Better Auth configured for:
   - Email/password
   - Google OAuth
2. Build `/login` and `/signup` pages
3. Build a `/auth/desktop-callback` page — this completes the loop back to
   the Electron app. On this page:
   - Confirm the user is authenticated
   - Generate a short-lived, single-use exchange code (**not** the raw
     session token)
   - Show a "Continue to Plaxio" button (do **not** auto-redirect — browsers
     block automatic custom-protocol redirects; this must be a user click)
   - On click, redirect to `plaxio://auth-callback?code=<exchange_code>`
4. Build a backend API route `/api/auth/exchange` that the desktop app calls
   with the exchange code to get back a real session token + refresh token.
   The exchange code must expire in under 60 seconds and be single-use.

### Desktop side (Electron main process only)

1. Register the custom protocol `plaxio://` in the Electron app
   (`app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient`)
2. Implement a "Sign In" flow: when triggered, open the system browser
   (`shell.openExternal`) to `https://plaxio.tech/login?desktop_redirect=true`
   — never open an embedded `BrowserWindow` for login
3. Handle the `plaxio://auth-callback` deep link: extract the exchange code,
   call `/api/auth/exchange` from the main process, receive session +
   refresh tokens
4. Store both tokens using Electron's `safeStorage` API (OS-native secure
   storage) — never localStorage, never plain files
5. Set `contextIsolation: true` and expose only a minimal, explicit IPC
   surface via `contextBridge` for the renderer to check "am I logged in"
   and "what's my plan/credits" — the renderer must never handle raw tokens
   directly
6. Implement token refresh logic: when the session token expires, use the
   refresh token silently in the main process to get a new one, no user
   interaction required
7. Implement "Sign Out": clear tokens from `safeStorage`, notify the
   renderer

Also implement a fallback: if the custom protocol fails to register on the
user's OS (rare but happens), fall back to a loopback HTTP server on
`127.0.0.1:<random port>` that the website can redirect to instead. Detect
which method to use automatically.

### Verification for Phase 1

I should be able to click "Sign In" in Plaxio, complete login in my real
browser, get redirected back into the app automatically, and see my
logged-in state persist across app restarts.

---

## Phase 2 — Credits / usage-based feature gating

1. Set up a Polar.sh account integration: products, a metered "AI
   generation credits" product, and the Credits/Meters feature (not a
   custom-built ledger)
2. Implement Polar webhook handling at `/api/webhooks/polar` — handle at
   minimum: `checkout.updated`, `subscription.created`,
   `subscription.updated`, `subscription.canceled`. Use ngrok or the Polar
   CLI forwarder for local testing.
3. Build a backend endpoint `/api/user/credits` that calls Polar's Customer
   State API and returns current plan + remaining credit balance for the
   logged-in user
4. In the Electron app, before any AI-driven action (code generation,
   simulation, HMI auto-generation), call this endpoint to check remaining
   credits. If insufficient:
   - Block the action
   - Show an in-app upgrade/top-up prompt that deep-links to
     `https://plaxio.tech/billing` (do not build in-app checkout — always
     hand off to the website for payment)
5. After a successful AI action that consumes credits, report usage back to
   Polar via their events/meter API so the balance stays accurate

### Verification for Phase 2

I should be able to see my credit balance reflected correctly in the app,
have an action blocked when credits run out, and see the balance update
within a few seconds of Polar's webhook firing after a top-up.

---

## Phase 3 — Website dashboard

Build `/dashboard` on the website (authenticated route) with:

1. Account overview: name, email, current plan
2. Usage section: credits remaining, recent usage history (pull from Polar
   Customer Meters API)
3. Billing section: current subscription status, "Manage Billing" button
   that redirects to Polar's hosted Customer Portal (do not build custom
   cancel/upgrade UI — Polar doesn't expose those APIs; the hosted portal is
   the correct pattern here)
4. Connected devices/sessions (nice-to-have, skip if time-constrained): list
   of desktop app sessions tied to the account, with a "revoke" action that
   invalidates that session's refresh token

Then, in the Electron app's **Settings panel**:

1. Add an "Account" section showing: logged-in email, current plan, credits
   remaining (pulled live from the `/api/user/credits` endpoint)
2. Add a "Manage Billing" button that opens `https://plaxio.tech/billing` in
   the system browser
3. Add "Sign Out"

---

## General rules

- Never store secrets, tokens, or Polar/Better Auth API keys in the
  Electron renderer or in any file that ships to users
- Never build custom subscription cancel/restore logic — always defer to
  Polar's hosted customer portal
- Use environment variables for all API keys, with a committed
  `.env.example`
- After each phase, summarize what was built, list any manual steps I need
  to do in the Polar dashboard or DNS settings, and wait for me to confirm
  before moving to the next phase

# Plaxio — Authentication, Credits & Billing Implementation

**Context for Claude Code:** I'm building Plaxio, an Electron-based industrial
automation IDE (VS Code fork), and need to add a full authentication + billing
system connecting the desktop app to a new marketing/account website.
Domain: `plaxio.tech`. Both the website and desktop app live in the same
monorepo root.

---

## Goal

Implement this in **3 phases, in order**. Complete and verify each phase
before starting the next one. Do not skip ahead.

- **Phase 1** — Authentication (desktop ⇄ website)
- **Phase 2** — Credits / usage-based feature gating
- **Phase 3** — Website dashboard (account, usage, billing)

---

## Tech stack (use these — don't substitute without asking)

- **Website:** Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind
- **Auth:** Better Auth (self-hosted, `npm: better-auth`), with the Better
  Auth Polar plugin for billing integration
- **Billing / credits:** Polar.sh (`npm: @polar-sh/sdk`, `@polar-sh/nextjs`)
  — use Polar's native Credits/Meters feature. Do **not** build a custom
  credits ledger from scratch.
- **Database:** Postgres (use whatever ORM already exists in the monorepo,
  or Prisma if none exists)
- **Desktop:** existing Electron app (VS Code fork) — add auth logic to the
  Electron **main process only**, never the renderer

---

## Monorepo structure

First, inspect the existing repo structure and **propose** (don't just
assume) where the new website should live — likely a new top-level
`website/` or `apps/web/` folder alongside the existing Electron app folder,
using a workspace tool (pnpm workspaces or turborepo — check what's already
configured, or recommend one if this is a fresh monorepo setup). Confirm
this structure before scaffolding if it's ambiguous.

---

## Phase 1 — Authentication

### Website side

1. Scaffold the Next.js website with Better Auth configured for:
   - Email/password
   - Google OAuth
2. Build `/login` and `/signup` pages
3. Build a `/auth/desktop-callback` page — this completes the loop back to
   the Electron app. On this page:
   - Confirm the user is authenticated
   - Generate a short-lived, single-use exchange code (**not** the raw
     session token)
   - Show a "Continue to Plaxio" button (do **not** auto-redirect — browsers
     block automatic custom-protocol redirects; this must be a user click)
   - On click, redirect to `plaxio://auth-callback?code=<exchange_code>`
4. Build a backend API route `/api/auth/exchange` that the desktop app calls
   with the exchange code to get back a real session token + refresh token.
   The exchange code must expire in under 60 seconds and be single-use.

### Desktop side (Electron main process only)

1. Register the custom protocol `plaxio://` in the Electron app
   (`app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient`)
2. Implement a "Sign In" flow: when triggered, open the system browser
   (`shell.openExternal`) to `https://plaxio.tech/login?desktop_redirect=true`
   — never open an embedded `BrowserWindow` for login
3. Handle the `plaxio://auth-callback` deep link: extract the exchange code,
   call `/api/auth/exchange` from the main process, receive session +
   refresh tokens
4. Store both tokens using Electron's `safeStorage` API (OS-native secure
   storage) — never localStorage, never plain files
5. Set `contextIsolation: true` and expose only a minimal, explicit IPC
   surface via `contextBridge` for the renderer to check "am I logged in"
   and "what's my plan/credits" — the renderer must never handle raw tokens
   directly
6. Implement token refresh logic: when the session token expires, use the
   refresh token silently in the main process to get a new one, no user
   interaction required
7. Implement "Sign Out": clear tokens from `safeStorage`, notify the
   renderer

Also implement a fallback: if the custom protocol fails to register on the
user's OS (rare but happens), fall back to a loopback HTTP server on
`127.0.0.1:<random port>` that the website can redirect to instead. Detect
which method to use automatically.

### Verification for Phase 1

I should be able to click "Sign In" in Plaxio, complete login in my real
browser, get redirected back into the app automatically, and see my
logged-in state persist across app restarts.

---

## Phase 2 — Credits / usage-based feature gating

1. Set up a Polar.sh account integration: products, a metered "AI
   generation credits" product, and the Credits/Meters feature (not a
   custom-built ledger)
2. Implement Polar webhook handling at `/api/webhooks/polar` — handle at
   minimum: `checkout.updated`, `subscription.created`,
   `subscription.updated`, `subscription.canceled`. Use ngrok or the Polar
   CLI forwarder for local testing.
3. Build a backend endpoint `/api/user/credits` that calls Polar's Customer
   State API and returns current plan + remaining credit balance for the
   logged-in user
4. In the Electron app, before any AI-driven action (code generation,
   simulation, HMI auto-generation), call this endpoint to check remaining
   credits. If insufficient:
   - Block the action
   - Show an in-app upgrade/top-up prompt that deep-links to
     `https://plaxio.tech/billing` (do not build in-app checkout — always
     hand off to the website for payment)
5. After a successful AI action that consumes credits, report usage back to
   Polar via their events/meter API so the balance stays accurate

### Verification for Phase 2

I should be able to see my credit balance reflected correctly in the app,
have an action blocked when credits run out, and see the balance update
within a few seconds of Polar's webhook firing after a top-up.

---

## Phase 3 — Website dashboard

Build `/dashboard` on the website (authenticated route) with:

1. Account overview: name, email, current plan
2. Usage section: credits remaining, recent usage history (pull from Polar
   Customer Meters API)
3. Billing section: current subscription status, "Manage Billing" button
   that redirects to Polar's hosted Customer Portal (do not build custom
   cancel/upgrade UI — Polar doesn't expose those APIs; the hosted portal is
   the correct pattern here)
4. Connected devices/sessions (nice-to-have, skip if time-constrained): list
   of desktop app sessions tied to the account, with a "revoke" action that
   invalidates that session's refresh token

Then, in the Electron app's **Settings panel**:

1. Add an "Account" section showing: logged-in email, current plan, credits
   remaining (pulled live from the `/api/user/credits` endpoint)
2. Add a "Manage Billing" button that opens `https://plaxio.tech/billing` in
   the system browser
3. Add "Sign Out"

---

## General rules

- Never store secrets, tokens, or Polar/Better Auth API keys in the
  Electron renderer or in any file that ships to users
- Never build custom subscription cancel/restore logic — always defer to
  Polar's hosted customer portal
- Use environment variables for all API keys, with a committed
  `.env.example`
- After each phase, summarize what was built, list any manual steps I need
  to do in the Polar dashboard or DNS settings, and wait for me to confirm
  before moving to the next phase

## Research Summary & Recommendation

Your proposed stack is solid and production-proven. Here's my validation and the exact architecture:

---

### Tech Stack — Confirmed ✅

| Layer | Tool | Why it's the right choice |
|---|---|---|
| **Auth** | Better Auth | Self-hosted, no vendor lock-in, native Polar plugin, supports custom token exchange flows |
| **Billing** | Polar.sh | Built for dev tools, native credits/meters, hosted customer portal (no PCI headaches), Better Auth plugin exists |
| **Website** | Next.js 15 App Router | Server components for dashboard, API routes for auth exchange + webhooks, Tailwind for fast UI |
| **DB** | Postgres + Prisma | Better Auth has a Prisma adapter, stores sessions/users/exchange codes |
| **Desktop auth** | Electron `safeStorage` + custom protocol | OS-native keychain, same pattern Cursor/VS Code use |

---

### Architecture Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  DESKTOP (Electron main process)                            │
│                                                              │
│  1. User clicks "Sign In"                                   │
│  2. shell.openExternal → plaxio.tech/login?desktop=true     │
│  3. Listens for plaxio://auth-callback?code=XXXXX           │
│  4. Calls POST plaxio.tech/api/auth/exchange {code}         │
│  5. Receives {sessionToken, refreshToken}                   │
│  6. Stores in safeStorage (OS keychain)                     │
│  7. IPC → renderer: {email, plan, credits}                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ↕ HTTPS
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WEBSITE (Next.js @ plaxio.tech)                            │
│                                                              │
│  /login, /signup → Better Auth (email + Google OAuth)       │
│  /auth/desktop-callback → generates exchange code → button  │
│  /api/auth/exchange → validates code → returns tokens       │
│  /api/user/credits → calls Polar Customer State API         │
│  /api/webhooks/polar → checkout, subscription events        │
│  /dashboard → account, usage, billing portal link           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ↕ API
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  POLAR.SH                                                    │
│                                                              │
│  Products: Plaxio Pro (subscription)                        │
│  Meters: AI Credits (usage-based)                           │
│  Customer Portal: billing management                         │
│  Webhooks → plaxio.tech/api/webhooks/polar                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Monorepo Structure Recommendation

Since your root `package.json` is VS Code's own build system and can't be modified, the website should be a **standalone Next.js app** in the repo:

```
plc-main/
├── src/                    # Electron/VS Code source
├── out/                    # Compiled Electron
├── vendor/                 # FUXA, etc
├── plaxio/                 # Marketing assets (existing)
├── website/                # ← NEW: Next.js app
│   ├── package.json
│   ├── prisma/
│   │   └── schema.prisma
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── app/
│   │   │   ├── login/
│   │   │   ├── signup/
│   │   │   ├── auth/desktop-callback/
│   │   │   ├── dashboard/
│   │   │   └── api/
│   │   │       ├── auth/[...all]/     # Better Auth handler
│   │   │       ├── auth/exchange/
│   │   │       ├── user/credits/
│   │   │       └── webhooks/polar/
│   │   └── lib/
│   │       ├── auth.ts               # Better Auth config
│   │       ├── polar.ts              # Polar SDK setup
│   │       └── db.ts                 # Prisma client
│   ├── .env.example
│   └── tailwind.config.ts
└── scripts/
```

No pnpm workspaces or turborepo needed — the two projects don't share code at build time. They communicate purely via HTTPS at runtime.

---

### Key Implementation Details

**Exchange code pattern** (prevents token theft):
- Website generates a random 64-char code, stores in DB with `expires_at = now + 60s`, `used = false`, `user_id`
- Desktop calls `/api/auth/exchange` with the code → server validates, marks used, returns real tokens
- If code is expired or already used → 401

**Token refresh** (silent, no user interaction):
- Session token: short-lived (15 min)
- Refresh token: long-lived (30 days)
- Electron main process runs a timer; on 401 from any API call, tries refresh automatically

**Credit check before AI actions:**
- Desktop calls `GET /api/user/credits` with session token
- Returns `{plan: "pro", credits: {remaining: 847, total: 1000}}`
- If `remaining <= 0` → block action, show upgrade prompt

---

### What You Need Before I Start

1. **Postgres** — Do you have one running (Supabase, Neon, Railway, local Docker)?
2. **Domain** — Is `plaxio.tech` already pointed to Vercel/somewhere, or do we develop on `localhost:3000` first?
3. **Polar.sh account** — Do you have one created at polar.sh, or should I factor in setup steps?
4. **Google OAuth** — Do you have a Google Cloud project with OAuth credentials, or skip Google for now and just do email/password?

Once you confirm these, I'll start Phase 1 implementation immediately.

}

## Assistant <sup>7/28/2026, 11:52:20 AM</sup>

Build passes. All routes are working. Now to wire up Supabase you need to:

1. Go to [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) → New project → Settings → API → copy your **Project URL** and **anon key**
2. Paste them into `website/.env.local`:
   ```
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://xxxx.supabase.co
   NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=eyJ...
   ```
3. In Supabase → Authentication → Providers → enable **Google** (needs Google OAuth client ID/secret from Google Cloud Console)
4. In Supabase → Authentication → URL Configuration → add `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback` as a redirect URL

The full flow is ready:
- `/login` → email/password or Google OAuth → redirects to `/dashboard`
- `/signup` → email/password (sends confirmation email) or Google OAuth
- `/dashboard` → protected, shows user info + plan
- `/api/auth/callback` → handles OAuth redirect from Supabase
- `/api/auth/signout` → signs out and redirects home

## Assistant <sup>7/28/2026, 12:00:13 PM</sup>

Dev server is up. The middleware error is fixed. Now here's what you need to do to complete the Supabase setup (takes ~5 minutes):

---

**Step 1 — Create Supabase project**
1. Go to [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) → New project → name it `plaxio`
2. Once created, go to **Settings → API** and copy:
   - Project URL → paste as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`
   - `anon` key → paste as `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
3. Update `website/.env.local` with those values

**Step 2 — Link CLI to your project**
Run this in your terminal (in the `website/` folder):
```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref YOUR_PROJECT_REF
supabase db push
```
(Project ref is in your Supabase dashboard URL: `supabase.com/dashboard/project/YOUR_REF`)

**Step 3 — Enable Google OAuth in Supabase**
1. Supabase dashboard → Authentication → Providers → Google → Enable
2. Add your Google OAuth Client ID + Secret (from [console.cloud.google.com](https://console.cloud.google.com))
3. Add redirect URL: `https://YOUR_PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`

**Step 4 — Add redirect URL in Supabase**
Authentication → URL Configuration → add:
```
http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback
```

Once `.env.local` has real values, `/login` and `/signup` will fully work with email/password and Google OAuth.

## Assistant <sup>7/28/2026, 12:06:08 PM</sup>

Yes — Supabase handles OAuth completely. You just need to give it your Google Client ID and Secret so it can do the OAuth dance on your behalf. Supabase hosts the callback endpoint (`https://impbakzawydocenlfrbx.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback`) — you don't write any OAuth code yourself.

The two steps:

         process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,
         { cookies: { getAll() { return cookieStore.getAll(); }, setAll(cookiesToSet) { try { cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) => cookieStore.set(name, value, options)); } catch {} } } }

     }

Exactly. The architecture is:

**Website** = billing, payments, account management, plan limits
**Desktop IDE** = consumes those limits, syncs state via API

3. Desktop periodically calls an API to check: remaining credits, plan tier, feature flags
4. When the user uses AI agents/completions in the IDE, it decrements usage via API
5. If limits are hit, IDE shows "upgrade" prompt that opens the website billing page
